passages.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiakim was king of Judah.
He ruled for three years.
Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem.
He surrounded Jerusalem.
He besieged the city.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ לְמַלְכ֖וּת יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֑ה בָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֥צַר עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, along with some of the articles from the house of God. He carried these off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, where he put them in the treasury of his god.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave Jehoiakim into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand.
Jehoiakim was king of Judah.
The Lord also gave Nebuchadnezzar some articles from the house of God.
Nebuchadnezzar took these articles to the land of Shinar.
He brought them to the house of his god.
He placed the articles in the treasury of his god.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י בְּיָד֜וֹ אֶת־ יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֗ה וּמִקְצָת֙ כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיְבִיאֵ֥ם אֶֽרֶץ־ שִׁנְעָ֖ר בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֑יו וְאֶת־ הַכֵּלִ֣ים הֵבִ֔יא בֵּ֖ית אוֹצַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility— young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
passages.sermon:
Nebuchadnezzar was the king of Babylon.
He spoke to Ashpenaz.
Ashpenaz was the chief of his court officials.
Nebuchadnezzar gave Ashpenaz a command.
He told Ashpenaz to bring some young men from Israel.
These young men came from the royal family and the nobility of Israel.
The king wanted young men with no physical defect.
He wanted them to be handsome.
He wanted them to be skilled in all wisdom.
He wanted them to be knowledgeable.
He wanted them to be quick to understand.
He wanted them to be able to serve in the king’s palace.
The king wanted Ashpenaz to teach these young men.
He wanted them to learn the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְאַשְׁפְּנַ֖ז רַ֣ב סָרִיסָ֑יו לְהָבִ֞יא מִבְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וּמִזֶּ֥רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה וּמִן־ הַֽפַּרְתְּמִֽים׃ יְלָדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין־ בָּהֶ֣ם כָּל־ מְאוּם וְטוֹבֵ֨י מַרְאֶ֜ה וּמַשְׂכִּילִ֣ים בְּכָל־ חָכְמָ֗ה וְיֹ֤דְעֵי דַ֙עַת֙ וּמְבִינֵ֣י מַדָּ֔ע וַאֲשֶׁר֙ כֹּ֣חַ בָּהֶ֔ם לַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּהֵיכַ֣ל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּֽלֲלַמְּדָ֥ם סֵ֖פֶר וּלְשׁ֥וֹן כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

passages.text: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.
passages.sermon:
The king gave the young men food and wine from his own table every day.
He decided what they would eat and drink each day.
He planned for them to be trained for three years.
After three years, some of them would serve before the king.
passages.original: וַיְמַן֩ לָהֶ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ דְּבַר־ י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֗וֹ מִפַּת־ בַּ֤ג הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וּמִיֵּ֣ין מִשְׁתָּ֔יו וּֽלְגַדְּלָ֖ם שָׁנִ֣ים שָׁל֑וֹשׁ וּמִ֨קְצָתָ֔ם יַֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
passages.sermon: Some of these young men came from the tribe of Judah.\r\nTheir names were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה דָּנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָֽה׃

passages.text: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
passages.sermon:
The chief official was in charge of the young men from Judah.
He gave them new names.
He gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar.
He gave Hananiah the name Shadrach.
He gave Mishael the name Meshach.
He gave Azariah the name Abednego.
passages.original: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם לָהֶ֛ם שַׂ֥ר הַסָּרִיסִ֖ים שֵׁמ֑וֹת וַיָּ֨שֶׂם לְדָֽנִיֵּ֜אל בֵּ֣לְטְשַׁאצַּ֗ר וְלַֽחֲנַנְיָה֙ שַׁדְרַ֔ךְ וּלְמִֽישָׁאֵ֣ל מֵישַׁ֔ךְ וְלַעֲזַרְיָ֖ה עֲבֵ֥ד נְגֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a young man from Judah.
Daniel decided something in his heart.
He decided he would not make himself unclean.
He would not eat the king’s food.
He would not drink the king’s wine.
Daniel asked the chief official for permission.
He asked not to make himself unclean.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שֶׂם דָּנִיֵּאל֙ עַל־ לִבּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־ יִתְגָּאַ֛ל בְּפַתְבַּ֥ג הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וּבְיֵ֣ין מִשְׁתָּ֑יו וַיְבַקֵּשׁ֙ מִשַּׂ֣ר הַסָּרִיסִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א יִתְגָּאָֽל׃

passages.text: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official, but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”
passages.sermon:
God gave Daniel favor.
God gave Daniel compassion.
The chief official saw this favor and compassion.
The chief official spoke to Daniel.
He said, “I am afraid of my lord the king.
The king gave you your food and drink.
If the king sees your faces looking worse than the other young men your age, he will be angry.
You would make me guilty before the king.
You would endanger my life.”
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ דָּ֣נִיֵּ֔אל לְחֶ֖סֶד וּֽלְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִפְנֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר הַסָּרִיסִֽים׃ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר שַׂ֤ר הַסָּרִיסִים֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל יָרֵ֤א אֲנִי֙ אֶת־ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִנָּ֔ה אֶת־ מַאֲכַלְכֶ֖ם וְאֶת־ מִשְׁתֵּיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֡ר לָמָּה֩ יִרְאֶ֨ה אֶת־ פְּנֵיכֶ֜ם זֹֽעֲפִ֗ים מִן־ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּגִֽילְכֶ֔ם וְחִיַּבְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־ רֹאשִׁ֖י לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a young man from Judah.
Daniel was living in Babylon.
The king of Babylon took Daniel and other young men from Judah.
The king wanted them to serve in his palace.
The chief official was in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The chief official appointed a steward over them.

Daniel spoke to the steward.
Daniel said, “Please test your servants for ten days.”
Daniel asked the steward to give them only vegetables to eat.
Daniel asked the steward to give them only water to drink.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר דָּנִיֵּ֖אל אֶל־ הַמֶּלְצַ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִנָּה֙ שַׂ֣ר הַסָּֽרִיסִ֔ים עַל־ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָֽה׃ נַס־ נָ֥א אֶת־ עֲבָדֶ֖יךָ יָמִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֑ה וְיִתְּנוּ־ לָ֜נוּ מִן־ הַזֵּרֹעִ֛ים וְנֹאכְלָ֖ה וּמַ֥יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a young man from Judah.
Daniel was living in Babylon.
Daniel and his friends did not want to eat the king’s food.
Daniel spoke to the steward.
The steward was in charge of Daniel and his friends.
Daniel said, “Look at us after ten days.”
“Look at our faces.”
“Look at the faces of the young men who eat the king’s food.”
“Compare our appearance with theirs.”
“Do what you think is right with your servants.”
passages.original: וְיֵרָא֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ מַרְאֵ֔ינוּ וּמַרְאֵה֙ הַיְלָדִ֔ים הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים אֵ֖ת פַּתְבַּ֣ג הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְאֵ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה עִם־ עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.
passages.sermon: The steward listened to Daniel and his friends.\r\nThe steward agreed to their request.\r\nThe steward tested them for ten days.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע לָהֶ֖ם לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְנַסֵּ֖ם יָמִ֥ים עֲשָׂרָֽה׃

passages.text: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.
passages.sermon:
Four young men chose not to eat the king’s food.
They ate only vegetables.
The steward gave them vegetables instead of the king’s food and wine.
After ten days, the steward looked at them.
Their appearance was good.
They looked healthy and strong.
They looked better than all the other young men.
The other young men ate the king’s food.
passages.original: וּמִקְצָת֙ יָמִ֣ים עֲשָׂרָ֔ה נִרְאָ֤ה מַרְאֵיהֶם֙ ט֔וֹב וּבְרִיאֵ֖י בָּשָׂ֑ר מִן־ כָּל־ הַיְלָדִ֔ים הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים אֵ֖ת פַּתְבַּ֥ג הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.
passages.sermon:
The steward managed the food and drink for the young men.
He did not give them the king’s choice food.
He did not give them the wine they were supposed to drink.
He gave them vegetables instead.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י הַמֶּלְצַ֗ר נֹשֵׂא֙ אֶת־ פַּתְבָּגָ֔ם וְיֵ֖ין מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְנֹתֵ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם זֵרְעֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.
passages.sermon:
God gave gifts to four young men.
God gave them knowledge.
God gave them understanding.
They understood every kind of literature.
They had wisdom.
Daniel was one of these four young men.
God gave Daniel special insight.
Daniel understood all kinds of visions.
Daniel understood all kinds of dreams.
passages.original: וְהַיְלָדִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אַרְבַּעְתָּ֔ם נָתַ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם הָֽאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַדָּ֥ע וְהַשְׂכֵּ֖ל בְּכָל־ סֵ֣פֶר וְחָכְמָ֑ה וְדָנִיֵּ֣אל הֵבִ֔ין בְּכָל־ חָז֖וֹן וַחֲלֹמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Now at the end of the time specified by the king, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
passages.sermon:
The king set a specific time for the young men to be brought before him.
The chief official was in charge of these young men.
The chief official brought the young men to King Nebuchadnezzar.
King Nebuchadnezzar saw the young men at the end of the appointed time.
passages.original: וּלְמִקְצָת֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לַהֲבִיאָ֑ם וַיְבִיאֵם֙ שַׂ֣ר הַסָּרִיסִ֔ים לִפְנֵ֖י נְבֻכַדְנֶצַּֽר׃

passages.text: And the king spoke with them, and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar spoke with the young men.
He compared all the young men who stood before him.
He found Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
He saw that no one else was equal to these four.
Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah stood out among all the others.
The king chose them to serve before him.
They entered the king’s service.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתָּם֮ הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וְלֹ֤א נִמְצָא֙ מִכֻּלָּ֔ם כְּדָנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָ֑ה וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
passages.sermon:
King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon.
He had young men brought before him.
Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah were among them.
The king asked them questions about wisdom and understanding.
He tested them in every matter of wisdom and understanding.
He compared them to all the magicians and enchanters in his kingdom.
He found Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters.
passages.original: וְכֹ֗ל דְּבַר֙ חָכְמַ֣ת בִּינָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ בִּקֵּ֥שׁ מֵהֶ֖ם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽיִּמְצָאֵ֞ם עֶ֣שֶׂר יָד֗וֹת עַ֤ל כָּל־ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּים֙ הָֽאַשָּׁפִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּכָל־ מַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
passages.sermon: Daniel was a wise and faithful servant in the king’s court.\r\nDaniel stayed in the royal court.\r\nDaniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל עַד־ שְׁנַ֥ת אַחַ֖ת לְכ֥וֹרֶשׁ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
